families.s: HSE foundry dust, molten-metal fume and respiratory-health guidance
families.t: ferrous fume, silica, spray mist, asthma, lung cancer, extraction, RPE, supervision, monitoring and health surveillance
f: Foundry workers can be exposed to molten-metal fume, spray mist and silica-containing dust.
Ferrous foundry fume can cause lung cancer.
Pattern-assembly fume and spray mist can cause occupational asthma or other lung disease.
Dry sand, fettling and kiln-lining dust can contain respirable crystalline silica.
Inhaling respirable crystalline silica can cause silicosis.
Mechanical controls such as extraction should be kept effective.
Administrative controls, supervision and worker compliance support sustained exposure control.
Records, exposure monitoring and health surveillance should demonstrate continuing control.
families.g: Foundry respiratory risk depends on metal and process, sand and lining materials, dust and fume generation, enclosure and extraction, RPE, task duration, maintenance, monitoring and worker susceptibility.

families.t: melting furnaces, charge, fume, extraction, furnace condition, refractory, maintenance, RPE and health monitoring
f: Foundry COSHH guidance includes a specific furnace-work control sheet.
Furnace work can generate hazardous molten-metal fume.
Fume extraction should capture emissions at the furnace where practicable.
Furnace charge and condition can affect fume generation.
Refractory inspection and relining work can introduce silica and other dust exposure.
Maintenance should preserve extraction and furnace integrity.
Suitable RPE may be required for residual exposure or exceptional tasks.
Health monitoring and records should support review of long-term respiratory risk.
families.g: Furnace-work risk depends on metal and charge, furnace design and temperature, fume and dust generation, extraction, refractory condition, maintenance, RPE, task duration and monitoring.

families.s: HSE foundry pouring, casting and cooling exposure-control guidance
families.t: molten metal, fume, splash, casting, cooling, distance, RPE, local controls, work positioning and supervision
f: Foundry COSHH guidance includes pouring, casting and cooling molten metal.
These tasks can generate molten-metal fume and splash.
Work positioning and distance should reduce direct exposure.
Local controls should minimise fume where practicable.
RPE may be required for residual fume exposure.
Moulds, ladles and implements should be dry and correctly prepared.
Screens or remote operation can reduce operator proximity to molten metal.
Safe procedures, training and supervision should cover pouring, cooling, abnormal events and PPE.
families.g: Pouring and casting risk depends on metal and temperature, mould and ladle condition, fume and splash, operator distance, extraction and screening, RPE and clothing, work method and supervision.

families.t: dry sand, respirable crystalline silica, reclamation, enclosure, dust extraction, cleaning, exposure monitoring, RPE and surveillance
f: Foundry COSHH guidance provides a specific control sheet for sand reclamation.
Dry foundry sand can release respirable crystalline silica.
Reclamation equipment should be enclosed where practicable.
Dust extraction should capture emissions from transfer and processing points.
Cleaning methods should avoid redistributing dry silica dust.
Exposure measurement should verify control where needed.
RPE may supplement engineering controls for residual or maintenance exposure.
Health surveillance is relevant where workers remain exposed to respirable crystalline silica.
families.g: Sand-reclamation risk depends on sand composition and moisture, process and transfer points, enclosure and extraction, cleaning, maintenance, exposure duration, RPE, monitoring and surveillance.

families.s: HSE foundry mould and core-making dust-and-chemical control guidance
families.t: sand, binders, core making, shell moulding, dust extraction, pattern assembly, formaldehyde, furanes, ventilation and surveillance
f: Foundry COSHH guidance includes mould and core making and shell moulding.
Sand handling can generate respirable crystalline silica.
Binders and process chemicals can create vapour and skin exposure.
Dust extraction should control emissions at mixing, filling and finishing points.
Pattern assembly may generate fume capable of causing asthma.
Foundry publications include guidance for formaldehyde and furanes.
Ventilation, containment and suitable PPE should reflect the binder and process.
Exposure monitoring and health surveillance should be considered for residual respiratory risk.
families.g: Mould and core-making risk depends on sand and binder chemistry, mixing and filling method, dust and vapour generation, extraction, skin contact, maintenance, monitoring and worker susceptibility.
